question: A student starts with 44 points. Michael and Rachel compare their scores. They lose 21 points to a failed quiz. They lose 19 points to a missed assignment. They lose 2 points to a rounding error. They add 7 points from extra credit. They multiply by 3 to project final grade. They multiply by 9 to forecast next semester. What is their next semester projection?

A manufacturer had 106 units. He multiplied by 8 for production factor. He multiplied by 4 for shift scaling. He multiplied by 4 for quality levels. He multiplied by 2 for expansion. He subtracted 6736 for major order (converting to adjusted units). Measured in adjusted production units. What was the adjusted production unit count?

A farm had 26 acres. They doubled the planted area. They added 78 acres from new purchases. They divided by 2 for crop rotation. They subtracted 35 acres for conservation. They added 20 more for expansion. Finally, they multiplied by 4 for a land management plan. One neighboring property had 50 acres but was not included. What is the final acreage?

Evan and Rose manage funds. They start with 82 dollars. They multiply by 4 (328). They add 5 (333). They lose 73 (260). They add 48 (308). They lose 164. Rose has 200 dollars. How much do they have combined?

In the morning a print shop ran off 168 posters on each of its 6 machines. Before lunch a courier delivered 56 posters printed elsewhere, and they joined the same stack. During the afternoon 261 posters were pasted up around the town. In the evening a cancelled order sent 56 posters back to the stack. The shop's front window is 3 metres wide. How many posters are on the stack at the end of the day?
A store had 39 items. They multiplied by 6. They multiplied by 4. They added 6 more. They removed 890. They divided by 4. About 25 items expired, which is unrelated. How many items remain?

A comic shop had 40 back-issue comics in a discount bin. A donation added 52 more comics. A collector bought 51 of them in one visit. A restock added 74 more comics. A convention weekend then tripled the tracked bin's comic count. A second surge of interest tripled it again. A separate long-box in the back room, unrelated to this bin, held 200 comics. How many comics were in the discount bin after the second surge?

A community garden started the season with 145 tomato seedlings. Nadia planted 66 more seedlings and Tariq planted 55, so Nadia planted more than Tariq. The garden is 30 metres long. Every seedling grew into a plant that produced 8 tomatoes, and a neighbour also gave the gardeners 71 tomatoes from her own vines. At the market every tomato the garden had was sold for 5 cents. How many cents did the garden take in?

On Monday morning a factory received 156 crates and divided them equally among its 4 assembly bays. Later that morning each crate in the first bay was opened and found to hold 5 machine parts. During the afternoon every part in that bay was fitted with 6 washers. In the evening a spare tin added 77 washers to the bay's stock. Each washer is dipped in 9 grams of grease before it goes on the line. How many grams of grease does the first bay need?

Kara collected 196 shells on the first day of her beach holiday, more than the 150 that her brother Finn collected. The beach is 3 kilometres long. On the second day she found 22 more shells, and on the third day 28. On the fourth day she found 75 shells, on the fifth day 58, and on the last day just 7. How many shells did Kara collect in total?

Mara planted 13 rows of carrots with 9 plants in every row. She later added 20 more seedlings to the same plot. She harvested 94 of the plants in August, rabbits destroyed 18 more, and she gave 4 plants to a neighbour. Her shed sits half a mile down the lane, and she has been gardening this plot for 15 years. Every plant still growing will produce 6 carrots. How many carrots can Mara still expect?

A dairy farm tracked the total liters of milk in its holding tank throughout the day, starting with 218 liters at dawn. During the morning milking, 140 liters were shipped out to the creamery. By midday, a cheese-making order multiplied the tank's tracked volume by 7. In the afternoon, a yogurt order multiplied it by 7 again. By evening, the milk was split evenly into 6 storage jugs, and only the first jug's volume was tracked from then on. By night, a spoilage check removed 61 liters from the tracked jug. How many liters were in the tracked jug by night?

A warehouse started with 158 items. They added 66 items from morning delivery. They multiplied by 7 for weekly tracking. They divided by 4 for four-location split. They multiplied by 3 for comprehensive inventory. They added 79 items from afternoon restocking. Finally, 43 items were removed for quality check. Using a morning-through-evening timeline, how many items are managed?

Vic's corner shop had 127 six-packs of juice, but sold 118 of them over the holiday weekend. Since a six-pack holds 6 cans, Vic counted what was left in cans. His rival Wen, whose shop is across the street, had 6 times as many cans of juice as Vic. Wen then received a delivery of 76 more cans. How many cans of juice did Wen have?

A wildlife group counted 224 nesting boxes across a woodland that covers 60 hectares. Half of the boxes stand on the north side, and the group surveyed that half only. Surveyors found 102 of the boxes they checked to be empty. Every box that was occupied held 4 chicks. Predators took 36 of those chicks over the following week. Each chick that survived was fitted with 3 coloured rings. How many coloured rings were used?

A farmer started with 95 kilograms of grain. He multiplied harvest by 4 times. He sold 16 kilograms at market. He purchased 8 kilograms of premium seed. He stored 21 more kilograms from another harvest. His grain was approximately 0.39 metric tons total. How many kilograms did he have?

Lisa and Mark are comparing their book collections. Lisa starts with 78 books. She adds 24 books from a donation. She adds 30 more books. She sells 84 books at a used bookstore. She buys 75 new books. She receives 36 books as a gift. Mark has collected books for 15 years. How many books does Lisa have now?

A dairy farm tracked the total gallons of milk in the morning collection tank, starting with 55 gallons at dawn. By mid-morning, a second herd's milking tripled the tracked volume. By midday, a third herd's milking multiplied the tracked volume by 9. By afternoon, a late collection added 65 more gallons. Converting the tracked volume from gallons to liters for the co-op's export report — a simple unit change — the farm multiplied the tracked number by 7 that evening. How many liters did the tracked total come to by evening?

Nora had 12 sheets of coloured paper. She used 10 of them for a school poster and gave 1 sheet to her brother. She cut every sheet she had left into 9 strips. She used 7 of the strips to make a paper chain. Then she cut each remaining strip into 5 small squares for confetti, and 1 square blew out of the window. How many squares of confetti does Nora have?

A business operates through the day. They start with 138 dollars in the morning. Daniel and Lisa compare their finances. They multiply by 7 to project for seven months. They lose 728 dollars to expenses. They lose 229 dollars to taxes. They multiply by 3 to triple for fiscal planning. They add 62 dollars from bonuses. The company opened 10 years ago. What is their annual projection?

Kofi began the mosaic project with 79 ceramic tiles. His sister Amara, whose box held more than his, gave him 70 tiles from her own supply. Every tile was then scored and snapped into 4 small squares. Amara handed over 59 loose squares she had already cut, and Kofi found 52 more squares in a tin under the bench. The competition itself ran for 6 hours. Each square placed in the mosaic is worth 9 points from the judges. How many points was Kofi's mosaic worth?

A farm produced 54 bushels day 1. Day 2 multiplied by 8 to 432. Day 3 multiplied by 7 to 3024. Day 4 multiplied by 9. A neighboring farmer contributed 67 bushels. They harvested a dozen apple trees that week. How many total bushels did they accumulate?

Yuki had 235 cents in her pocket, spent 194 cents on a bus ticket, and then found 20 cents on the floor of the bus. Her brother Zane had 4 times as many cents as Yuki had after that, so Zane was the richer of the two. Zane then earned 73 cents returning bottles and 63 cents sweeping a neighbour's path, which took him about a dozen minutes. Zane counts his money in cents rather than dollars, knowing that one hundred cents make a dollar. How many cents does Zane have now?

A brewery had 239 crates of bottles, but 33 crates were damaged in transit. The brewery has 15 staff. Each crate holds 7 boxes, and each box holds 6 bottles. During the festival the brewery sold 7681 bottles. It then tripled its remaining stock with a new batch. How many bottles did the brewery have in stock?

A farm had 181 eggs collected by morning. They added 69 more from afternoon collection. They divided the total equally by 5 for packaging. They added 41 eggs from evening laying. They removed 14 eggs that cracked. The farm had 8 chickens producing eggs. How many eggs were ready for sale?
